[[Barb Howard]] - mother |affiliation = |role = |TV actor =[[Teagan Meredith]] |dob =April 14, [[Timeline#2065|2065]] |dob verified=yes |age =12 (2077) |age verified=yes }} '''Janey Howard''' is the daughter of [[Barb Howard|Barbara]] and [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]], born in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era. She appears {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Janey was born to [[The Ghoul|Cooper]] and [[Barb Howard]] on April 14, [[Timeline#2065|2065]].[[Robert House]]: ''"The date of the end of the world may not interest you, Mr. Howard. But the date the data coalesced might. April 14th, 2065, at 5:17 a.m. Is that date of any interest to you?"''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"That's my daughter's birthday."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) After her parents divorced, Janey spent her time with her father, participating in his gig work as an assistant. On October 23, 2077, the 12 year old Janey was with Cooper on a gig at a birthday party near [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]], where he taught her the joke method of using her thumb to tell how far away a nuclear explosion is. Shortly after, Janey was the first one at the party to witness the bombs falling on the city below. She fled with Cooper on [[horse]]back as Los Angeles was destroyed. At some point around late 2077, Janey and her mother were designated as occupants for cryo-stasis chambers in the [[Las Vegas management Vault|management Vault]] below [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]],{{FOTV|2|5}} though it is unknown if either of them ever arrived there and used them. Barb was known to have entered the facility at one point, though the only evidence of this is a [[Colorado]] postcard she placed in her cryo chamber as a message for her husband.{{FOTV|2|8}} ==In the ''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Head]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Trap]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Radio]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Innovator]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Profligate]]=== Janey does not appear in this episode, but she is briefly seen in a family picture of the Howards while Barb is attempting (and failing) to put Janey's teddy bear into her Vault-Tec suitcase of keepsakes. ===[[The Wrangler]]=== While not directly appearing, [[Robert House]] explains to [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] that Janey's birth coincided with his computer algorithms for determining the end of the world occurred on her birthday - April 14, 2065. Both Janey and Barbara Howard are revealed to be in cryo-stasis within the underground Vault-Tec management Vault in [[New Vegas]]. [[Hank MacLean]] uses both Janey and Barbara as leverage to trade The Ghoul for [[Lucy MacLean]]. In Barb's office in the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]], [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] finds a picture of Janey on Barb's desk. ===[[The Strip]]=== In the [[Las Vegas management Vault]], the Ghoul finds Barb and Janey's cryo pods and has [[Robert House]] open them. However, they are both empty. On the floor of Barb's pod is a Colorado postcard with a message reading "Colorado was a good idea," referencing her husband's idea that they go there before he was arrested. With relief, the Ghoul tells House that for the first time in 200 years, he knows that his family is still alive. ==Notes== In the [[The End script|script for "The End,"]] Janey was stated to be six years old; this was shown not to be the case in the season 2 episode "The Wrangler."{{inline quote|Cooper’s daughter JANEY (6) proudly cheers from the sidelines. She also wears full rodeo garb.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 2}} Other ages listed in the script, including that of [[Steph Harper]], also differ from what is seen in the show. ==Appearances== Janey Howard appears only {{In|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|3=103|6=106|7=107|9=201}} ==Behind the scenes== Prior to the release of Season 1, actor Avery Reed was listed on IMDB as playing "Young Janey," in addition to [[Teagan Meredith]] playing Janey herself. However, in all scenes for both Season 1 and 2, Janey has only ever been played by Teagan Meredith; Avery Reed is not credited in any episode, and was also removed from IMDB's credits some time before the release of Season 2 in December 2025. ===Season 2 deleted scene=== [[File:FOTV S2E6 Lisa Joy deleted scene 3.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Lisa Joy]] speaking to [[Ella Purnell]] and Teagan Meredith at the adobe church's film set]] In January 2026, after the release of "[[The Other Player]]," director [[Lisa Joy]] posted an Instagram story featuring a behind the scenes clip of the film set for the [[adobe church]], where the Ghoul is taken in the episode. This clip seems to evidence a scene that was cut from the episode, as it includes Joy talking to [[Ella Purnell]] and Teagan Meredith in their roles as [[Lucy MacLean]] and Janey Howard, neither of whom appear at the church in the final release. Janey otherwise does not appear in this episode, and Teagan Meredith is not credited in it. The Instagram story is no longer available and does not appear to have been preserved, but some photos from it are still available (see on the right). In contemporaneous interviews, [[Walton Goggins]] mentioned that a scene from Season 2 in which the Ghoul "had to think about" Janey was cut due to an emotional breakdown he suffered because of his exhaustion and feelings at being away from his own son during filming for that scene. Goggins' description seems to match this scene at the church, though this has not explicitly been confirmed.[[Walton Goggins]]: ''"And there's a sequence of events, but was so physically taxing that over the course of doing it, there was a scene that actually didn't make it into the show, so no one will ever see it. But a scene where- I won't tell you if the person was there or not- but a scene where [the Ghoul] had to think about his child, you know, and I was so exhausted and so open and so vulnerable and filled with so much shame about not being around my own child. You know, I missed him so terribly that this moment kind of came, and it all came out, like, and I couldn't stop it. I literally, it made everyone so uncomfortable, but it was transcendent, right? That's what we do this for. And, but it was, I think it was too much for our story, but it does. That's how it affects you."''
